title: Exact static exchange benchmark for the uniform electron gas: Dynamic-kernel tests and exchange-correlation cancellation near 2kF
abstract: The static local field factors of the uniform electron gas are known accurately from quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) calculations, but two of their most striking features have lacked a mechanism: $G_+$ grows almost exactly as $q^2$ up to nearly $2k_F$, and the violent $2k_F$ physics of the Fermi surface leaves only a faint trace in it. Combining the textbook first-order local-field relation with the exact static exchange polarizability gives a compact exact benchmark: the universal exchange-only local field factor $G_x(q,0) = -I(Q)Q^2/L(Q)^2$, $Q = q/2k_F$, with exact values $(1/4)(q/k_F)^2$ at small $q$, $π^2/6$ at $2k_F$ -- apparently never before stated as a local-field value -- and $1/3$ at large $q$, giving the exchange-only spin-averaged contact value $g(0) = 1/2$ of the unpolarized gas (BDL 1977). $G_x$ rises to a finite maximum of 1.9924 at $1.9685k_F$ and passes through $π^2/6$ at exactly $2k_F$ with a slope diverging as $\ln^3|q-2k_F|$. Against this benchmark, the 1980 BDL tabulation is accurate to about one percent below $1.5k_F$, while the 2024 McLachlan-variational kernel of Nazarov and Silkin is two-percent accurate only below $0.5k_F$, is a factor of 1.74 low at $2k_F$, and its large-q limit is inconsistent with the contact constraint. A spin-resolved decomposition of QMC local field factors about the exact baseline shows that, within the resolution and smoothness assumptions of the QMC-based representations, both features follow from a strong exchange-correlation cancellation: at the QMC point closest to $2k_F$ ($q = 2.01k_F$, $r_s = 2$), correlation cancels 0.43(7) of the exact exchange value 1.33. Computed consistently at each wavevector, the static exchange-kernel thresholds derived from the closed form reproduce, to 0.2%, the finite-wavevector charge threshold $r_s \approx 10.6$ near $q = 1.94k_F$ obtained numerically in 1980, and recovered again in 2014.
summary: This work establishes an exact theoretical benchmark for the static exchange-only local field factor in the uniform electron gas. By deriving this universal function, the authors critically test and demonstrate the quantitative failures of several established approximations (like BDL or McLVP) near the Fermi surface singularity at $2k_F$. The findings illuminate that observed physical behavior is governed by a precise cancellation between correlation and exchange effects.
main_problem: To establish an exact, universal benchmark for the static local field factors of the uniform electron gas (UEG), particularly addressing unexplained features near $2k_F$.
main_result: The paper derives and presents the exact exchange-only local field factor, $G_x(q,0)$, which shows specific limiting behaviors ($q^2/4$ at small $q$, $\pi^2/6$ at $2k_F$, and $1/3$ at large $q$).
method: The authors combine textbook local-field relations with exact static exchange polarizabilities derived from QMC calculations to construct a closed-form, universal benchmark.
model_or_system: The system is the Uniform Electron Gas (UEG), analyzed in the static limit ($\omega=0$) using density functional theory concepts applied to correlation functions.
key_observables: Static local field factors ($G^+$), the exchange-only factor $G_x(q,0)$, and spin-resolved components of these factors.
important_parameters: The wavevector $q$, normalized by $2k_F$ (using variable $Q$), and the density parameter $r_s$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that QMC representations are smooth enough to reveal underlying systematic cancellations between correlation and exchange contributions.
figures_summary: Figures compare the exact universal $G_x(q,0)$ against approximations from older theoretical kernels (BDL, McLVP), showing significant quantitative discrepancies in the comparison plots.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem by noting unexplained features in QMC data; it then derives the exact benchmark formula for $G_x$; subsequently, it rigorously compares this benchmark against established approximations and analyzes the underlying cancellation mechanisms near $2k_F$.
why_interesting:
While focused on electron gas theory, the rigorous benchmarking of correlation effects at finite momentum ($q 
eq 0$) provides fundamental insights into how screening modifies particle interactions, which is crucial for understanding correlated materials.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Preview of the paper’s central result. The exact, universal static exchange-only local field factor Gx(q,0) (black, Eq. (5), derived in Section II) compared with the full G+(q,0) at rs = 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 from the Kaplan-Kukkonen QMC-consistent representation [4] (colored; same rs values and color coding as Fig. 4). Exchange alone produces a sharp peak near 2kF of magnitude 1.99, more than twice the height of the full result at every density shown, while the full G+ curves are mutually close and nearly flat across the whole band 0 ≤ q ≤ 2kF. Sections II–III establish Gx exactly and benchmark existing dynamic exchange kernels against it; Section IV works out the linear-response...

Fig. 2. Top: the exact universal static exchange-only local field factor Gx(q,0), Eq. (5) (solid), compared with the Nazarov-Silkin McLVP exchange kernel [14] (dashed; rs = 2 data shown, but both curves are universal). Open circles: the 1980 BDL tabulation (ν = 0 row of their Table I [9]). The exact value π2/6 at 2kF is marked; horizontal dotted lines show the exact large-q limit 1/3 and the McLVP limit 1/2. Bottom: Gx/(q/kF)2, showing the exact rise from the compressibility-sum-rule value 1/4 to π2/24 at 2kF; the exact kernel is far from flat.

Fig. 3. Static local-kernel instability thresholds built from the exact adiabatic exchange kernel, Eq. (8), computed consistently at each wavevector from the exact closed form, Eq. (5). Spin channel (blue): minimum rs = 4.97 at q = 1.83kF; the dash-dotted line marks the Bloch transition rs = 5.45, and the dotted blue line the q →0 limit of the spin/proper-polarization condition, πα = 6.029, which is also the Hartree-Fock compressibility sign change; the charge condition has no long-wavelength solution. Charge channel (red): defined where Gx > 1 (1.60kF < q < 2.05kF), minimum rs = 10.62 at q = 1.944kF, in agreement with the numerical minimum rs ≈ 10.6 near q = 1.94kF of BDL Fig. 2 [9]...

Fig. 4. Spin-resolved decomposition of the Kaplan-Kukkonen static local field factors [4] about the exact exchange baseline, Eq. (5), for rs = 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. Top: parallel-spin correlation contribution G↑↑c = (G+ + G−)/2 − Gx. Bottom: antiparallel-spin local field factor G↑↓= (G+ − G−)/2, which is pure correlation and shows no 2kF structure within the resolution and smoothness assumptions of the KK representation.
